name: Yacolt
seo_title: Yacolt Christmas Events for Kids in Yacolt, WA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Yacolt, WA: the town tree lighting with Santa, Christmas trains on the Chelatchie Prairie Railroad and a family tree farm.
lede: Yacolt is a small town in the foothills of Clark County, Washington, and its Christmas season is built around a tall lit tree, a volunteer run train and a working farm.
celebrates: Yacolt celebrates Christmas the small town way. The Town of Yacolt hosts a Saturday tree lighting in early December, with an afternoon of activities, a visit from Santa and the lighting of a living Douglas fir that stands about 130 feet tall. Just outside town, the Chelatchie Prairie Railroad runs Christmas excursion trains through the forest, and a nearby farm opens for families who want a tree, a wagon ride and a warm drink. Together they give families around Vancouver, Battle Ground and Camas a short country drive for an evening of lights.
lastyear: Last year the tree lighting fell on the first Saturday of December, with the afternoon program leading up to Santa and the lighting after dark. The Clark County Today story on local tree lightings and the Town of Yacolt's own event page describe the same format, so families can expect a similar day this time. Check the Town of Yacolt page before you go, since start times for individual activities can shift.
facts: The town sits where the 1902 Yacolt Burn ended, and its name is often said to mean haunted place or place of the evil spirit. It was platted in 1903 when the railroad arrived and incorporated in 1908. The tree lighting is held in town, and the Chelatchie Prairie Railroad departs from the Yacolt depot. Parking is easiest if you arrive early, and winter evenings in the foothills are cold, so bring warm layers.
trains: The Chelatchie Prairie Railroad is an all volunteer line that runs excursion trains from May through December out of Yacolt. In the Christmas season it runs Santa trains, and the railroad's own site sells tickets. The line follows an old logging and passenger route through forest and over a trestle, a good ride for kids who love trains. Rally Takes the Train has a guide to the railroad, tickets and what to expect.

traditions: The Town of Yacolt lights a tall living Douglas fir on a Saturday in early December, after an afternoon of activities.
Santa comes to the tree lighting in the early evening, before the tree is lit.
Volunteers run Santa trains from the Yacolt depot through the forest in December.
A family farm near Yacolt opens in the Christmas season for trees and visits.
kidfact: In Yacolt, the tree that gets lit is not cut down. It is a living Douglas fir that keeps growing all year, and it reaches about 130 feet.
faq: Where is the Yacolt Christmas tree lighting?

The Town of Yacolt holds its tree lighting in town on a Saturday in early December. The activity day builds to a visit from Santa and then the lighting of the living tree. The Town of Yacolt website lists the current schedule and location.
Can kids ride a Christmas train in Yacolt?
Yes. The Chelatchie Prairie Railroad runs Santa trains out of Yacolt in December. The railroad is run by volunteers and sells its tickets online, and trains can sell out, so book ahead.
Why is the town called Yacolt?
A commonly told origin says the name comes from a Native word meaning haunted place or place of the evil spirit. The town grew up around the railroad after 1903 and incorporated in 1908.
How far is Yacolt from Vancouver and Portland?
Yacolt is a country drive northeast of Vancouver, Washington, and a bit farther from Portland. Plan extra time on winter evenings and dress warmly for the outdoor events.
